rv.q: But, although this is a perfectly creditable revival, it never achieves the right ecstatic quality. Synge's play is part of the problem. In 1907 it caused riots at the Abbey theatre , not least because it shows how Christy Mahon achieves the status of a sex-symbol when it is assumed he has killed his father.

In truth, it’s a bit flat in parts, but Sheehan, while he doesn’t have the overlarding comic charm of Cillian Murphy in the role (the last great playboy, for the Druid Theatre Company) or the accumulating swagger of Stephen Rea many moons ago, is perfectly beguiling and watchable.
